implementationAnalyses.conciseReason: The Content Agent document (finalAuthoringContract) contains a grounded 'Hero Video' block (componentId: component-001, canonicalBlockName: hero-video, selector: div.herovideo) with a four-cell single-row table structure. The authored table header is 'Hero Video' and the single row contains four cells: [video asset], [heading text], [primary CTA link], [secondary CTA link]. The live page confirms the block renders at div.herovideo with computed rect {x:0, y:64, width:780, height:438.75} — a full-width video hero immediately below the header. The section-metadata for this section supplies subtitles, poster, and transcript as section-level configuration (not block-row cells), which is consistent with EDS section-metadata conventions and must be preserved. The block does not exist in the repository inventory (blocks/ contains: cards, columns, footer, fragment, header, hero, widget — no hero-video). Therefore a new block must be created at blocks/hero-video/hero-video.js and blocks/hero-video/hero-video.css. The JS decorator must: (1) read the four authored cells — video link/asset, heading, primary CTA anchor, secondary CTA anchor; (2) build a native HTML5 <video> element using the video cell href as src, with poster/subtitles sourced from section-metadata on the parent section element (keys: poster, subtitles, transcript) so they remain configurable; (3) render the heading as an <h1> or <h2> (the live page shows the herovideo block text includes the heading inline, not as a separate DOM heading, so the decorator must promote it); (4) render the two CTA anchors with their captured accessible aria-label values (aria-label='PLAY FULL VIDEO about DISNEY IMAGINATION CAMPUS - STUDENT TRAVEL REIMAGINED' and aria-label='LEARN MORE about DISNEY IMAGINATION CAMPUS - STUDENT TRAVEL REIMAGINED' are present in the live computed samples — the decorator must set aria-label on each anchor using the heading text appended to the link label, matching the live pattern); (5) support keyboard play/pause via Enter and Space on the video element, matching the captured helper text 'Press Enter or Space to play or pause the video.' and the accessibility criterion; (6) render a visually-hidden helper text element containing that exact string for screen-reader context. The CSS must not hardcode color, typography, spacing, hover, or animation values that were listed as uncaptured — only structural layout rules (position, display, width) are safe to author. The section-metadata block (style: full-width, video-container; subtitles; poster; transcript) is already grounded in the Content Agent document and must be read by the JS decorator from the parent section's dataset or child section-metadata block — no new section-metadata authoring is required. The Cards (overlay) block (component-002) is a separate block in the same section and is out of scope for this story.

implementationAnalyses.conciseReason: The Content Agent document (finalAuthoringContract) contains a grounded block entry for 'Cards (overlay)' with canonicalBlockName 'cards' and selector 'div.cards.overlay'. This is the authoritative source for the block structure. The authored table shows a collection model where each row represents one category item with three cells: an image cell (nested object, not captured), a heading cell with the category label, and a third cell (nested object, not captured — likely a link). The live page confirms the rendered block as 'div.cards overlay block size-4 clickable overlay-animation' containing exactly four items: PERFORMING ARTS, ARTS & HUMANITIES, SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY, LEADERSHIP & INNOVATION. The source text also reveals that link targets were captured in the live scan (e.g., https://main--disneycampus--twdc-minnie.aem.live/programs/performing-arts and https://main--disneycampus--twdc-minnie.aem.live/programs/arts-humanities) for the first two rows, confirming the third cell is a link. The repository already has blocks/cards/cards.js and blocks/cards/cards.css (boilerplate implementation). The story requires implementing the 'overlay' variant of the existing cards block. The existing cards.js uses a collection model (each row → li, children → div.cards-card-image or div.cards-card-body). The overlay variant needs: (1) the JS decorator to handle the overlay variant's three-column structure (image, label heading, link), (2) CSS for the overlay variant styling. The acceptance criteria require exactly four items with the captured labels, each as a keyboard-reachable interactive link with accessible name matching the visible label. The block must NOT introduce additional content not in evidence. The implementation extends the existing cards block with an overlay variant rather than creating a new block, consistent with the Content Agent's canonicalBlockName 'cards' and authoredLabel 'Cards (overlay)'.

implementationAnalyses.conciseReason: The repository already contains blocks/header/header.js and blocks/header/header.css at branch migration-epic-001. The existing header.js implements the canonical AEM EDS fragment-based nav pattern: it reads a 'nav' metadata key (defaulting to /nav), loads that path as a fragment via loadFragment(), then maps the first three child sections of the fragment to nav-brand, nav-sections, and nav-tools grid areas. The existing header.css provides the full nav grid layout, hamburger, brand, sections (with nav-drop dropdowns), and tools areas. The live site evidence confirms the header block is already loaded (blocks/header/header.css is in the stylesheet list) and the rendered header-wrapper/nav-wrapper/nav#nav DOM is present with height 64px matching --nav-height. The Content Agent document does NOT include a header block table — the header is a global shared component loaded via the fragment convention (/nav document), not a per-page authored block. Per the CONTENT GAP & UNGROUNDED BLOCK RULES, this is a global pattern handled via the standard EDS header/nav fragment convention, not a hallucinated block table. The implementation plan therefore is: (1) modify blocks/header/header.js to add a nav-contact area that renders the captured contact bar content (Questions?, Call (321) 939 7560, Contact Us) from the nav fragment's fourth child section or from a dedicated contact row in the nav document, and to expose the header as a proper <header> landmark with role='banner'; (2) update blocks/header/header.css to add the nav-contact grid area and its layout without hardcoding uncaptured color/spacing tokens; (3) provide a /nav plain-HTML authoring template (drafts/nav.plain.html) so the Content Agent can author the nav document with the four sections: brand, sections (primary nav), tools (search), and contact. The nav document content model follows the existing EDS fragment convention: section 1 = brand (logo link), section 2 = primary nav list (ABOUT US, CURRICULUM & TICKETS, SPECIAL EVENTS, PLAN YOUR TRIP, CONNECT WITH US with sub-items), section 3 = tools (search), section 4 = contact bar (Questions? text, phone link, Contact Us link). All link destinations are left as configurable placeholders (#) because destination URLs were not captured. No typography, color, spacing, hover, or motion values are hardcoded beyond what is already present in the existing header.css. The --nav-height CSS custom property (64px, confirmed by computed rect height) is already defined in styles/styles.css and reused. The nav landmark already has id='nav' and aria-expanded in the existing JS; the implementation adds aria-label='Main navigation' to the nav element and wraps the contact bar in a <div class='nav-contact'> with appropriate accessible link names to satisfy the accessibility criteria.
